_metadata.description: Tier-1 static analyzers for embedded-schema layout and idempotency: centralized schema, non-idempotent DDL, ALTER-in-schema, unwired EnsureSchemas, non-per-domain schema, non-empty system schema, and cross-domain hard foreign keys. Go-only; runs when code-facts classifies the API as Go.

requirements.title: Centralized-schema detection
requirements.description: Detect a centralized/shared schema instead of per-domain embedded schema and emit SCHEMA_CENTRALIZED (L1, ERROR). Per-domain embedded schema is the substrate convention storage-health enforces and dogfoods.

validation.notes: A single central schema.sql produces SCHEMA_CENTRALIZED; per-domain embedded schemas do not.

requirements.title: Idempotency and ALTER analyzers
requirements.description: Detect non-idempotent DDL (SCHEMA_NOT_IDEMPOTENT, L1) and ALTER statements in embedded schema (SCHEMA_HAS_ALTER, L1) — both ERROR. ALTER belongs in a migration, not the embedded CREATE-only schema; non-idempotent DDL breaks re-run safety.

validation.notes: A CREATE TABLE without IF NOT EXISTS produces SCHEMA_NOT_IDEMPOTENT.
An ALTER TABLE in embedded schema produces SCHEMA_HAS_ALTER.

requirements.title: EnsureSchemas wiring analyzer
requirements.description: Detect when embedded schema exists but database.EnsureSchemas is not wired at startup and emit ENSURE_SCHEMAS_NOT_WIRED (L1, WARNING, autofixable). Without the wiring the schema is never applied.

validation.notes: A scenario with schema.sql but no EnsureSchemas call produces ENSURE_SCHEMAS_NOT_WIRED.

requirements.title: Per-domain, system-schema, and cross-domain-FK analyzers
requirements.description: Detect schema that is not split per-domain (SCHEMA_NOT_PER_DOMAIN, L3, gated on >=2 code-facts domains), tables placed in the system schema (SYSTEM_SQL_NOT_EMPTY, L3), and cross-domain hard foreign keys (CROSS_DOMAIN_HARD_FK, L3). All are WARNING-level structural findings.

validation.notes: A scenario with two code-facts domains sharing one schema produces SCHEMA_NOT_PER_DOMAIN; a single-domain scenario does not.
A foreign key crossing domain boundaries produces CROSS_DOMAIN_HARD_FK.
